title.narrative: Enhanced implementation of social protection strategy and reforms

description.narrative: Lebanon’s Social protection system suffers from gaps in coverage, comprehensiveness and adequacy. With the European Union (EU)’s contribution, ILO and UNICEF have provided technical support to develop, revise and adopt the National Social Protection Strategy (NSPS). Furthermore, the technical support to the Ministry of Social Affairs (MoSA) led for the design of the National Disability Allowance (NDA). During this biennium, ILO will prioritize the launch and operationalization of the NSPS, to be followed by the development of the implementation, financing and monitoring and evaluation (M&E) plans as well as the gradual establishment of Government-led institutional coordination structures at the inter-ministerial level and across the NSPS’ pillars. Additionally, ILO will prioritize the implementation of the pilot of the Social Protection Academy in 2024, addressing capacity-building gaps in inclusive social protection among government and non-government stakeholders, namely stakeholders in charge of coordination of the sector and the implementation of the SP strategy. Support for the Rights and Access program will continue – with a specific focus on the upgrade and development of the Disability Registry. ILO will also continue supporting the institutionalization of the NDA. Key elements of this model would include Institutional anchoring & program steering; Fund flows and financial management; implementation of the operational cycle (selection and identification, enrolment, payment, complaints, updates and exit); M&E and Audit. On the social health protection front, the ILO will conduct assessments and studies, in collaboration with relevant partners, to support funds’ efforts to redesign their health benefit packages and/or adjust their purchasing mechanisms with a view towards cost-containment and quality of care.
